sources.entry: PushNotifications - macOS app to test push notifications on iOS and Android.

summary.one_liner: A desktop app for sending test push notifications to iOS (APNs) and Android (FCM) devices.
summary.what_it_does: PushNotifications is a desktop utility for testing push notifications. For iOS it can authenticate to APNs either with a provider certificate (a .p12 file, with optional passphrase) or with an authentication token (a .p8 key plus key ID and team ID). For Android it sends messages through Firebase Cloud Messaging using a server key. For each send you supply a bundle ID, device token, JSON message payload and environment, and the app saves its settings automatically. The README says it runs on macOS, Windows and Linux. It is built with Electron and uses node-apn under the hood. The README also describes a "Push Hero" macOS app by the same author, which is a separate project.
use_cases: Test iOS push notifications during app development
Send test FCM messages to Android devices
Debug APNs certificate or token authentication
Send JSON notification payloads to a device token
Verify push setup before shipping an app
how_to_run: Download the latest release from the project's releases page (link not given in the README text)
Run `npm install` in the project root
Optionally run `npm start` to launch the app
Run `npm run dist` to produce installers with electron-builder
Output goes to the `dist` folder; you can only build for the OS you are currently running
notable: Supports both APNs provider certificate (.p12) and authentication token (.p8) methods
Covers Android FCM with a server key in the same tool
Cross-platform build via electron-builder (macOS, Windows, Linux)
caveats: Provider certificates expire yearly and must be regenerated and re-uploaded; tokens do not expire
Each installer type can only be built on its matching OS
On macOS Catalina and later, the unsigned app must be opened manually through System Settings' Security & Privacy
